data.gender_notes: Jamieson is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Scottish name Iain Mhòir (John the Great), which was a nickname for a large or important John. In turn, John is derived from the Hebrew name Yehohanan, which means 'God is gracious'. Therefore, Jamieson can be interpreted as 'Son of the God Who is Gracious'. The name Jamieson carries the meaning “Son of James” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jamieson usually hope their child will grow to embody son of james and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Iamason
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin form of the name Jamieson is Iamason. This name has been derived from the English name Jamieson, which is a combination of 'Jamie' (supplanting the original 'James') and the Scottish suffix '-son' (meaning 'son of').

in_english.name: Jamieson
